newsitem.title: JAPAN: NCB says leaving Feb long-term prime unchanged.
newsitem.headline: NCB says leaving Feb long-term prime unchanged.

text.p: Nippon Credit Bank Ltd (NCB) said on Thursday it would leave its long-term prime lending rate for February unchanged at a record-low 2.5 percent.
NCB also said it would raise the coupon rate of its February five-year debentures sold to institutional investors to 2.35 percent from 2.15 percent for its January debentures, effective Friday.

"The decision to raise the coupon rate by 0.2 percentage points was based on our desire to better reflect market trends, if even to a small degree, and also to provide better services to our customers," an NCB spokesman said. percent, was offered at 4.0 percent in the secondary market on Wednesday.
The spread between the coupon rate of February NCB debentures and Industrial Bank of Japan (IBJ) debentures will widen to 0.75 percent, up from 0.55 percent previously.
The IBJ debenture is the market benchmark.
The long-term prime lending rate is applied to loans of one year and longer to a long-term credit bank"s most creditworthy clients.
The Industrial Bank of Japan Ltd, the largest of Japan"s three long-term credit banks, said on Wednesday it would also leave its long-term prime lending rate for February unchanged at 2.5 percent.
